prompt: A straight line is used for data that clearly curves, and it's poor on training and test data alike.
tells: poor on training and test data alike
why: A straight line can't follow a curve, so it does poorly even on the training data. A model too simple for the pattern is underfitting.
trap: Overfitting would be good on training data.

prompt: The model predicts the same price for every house.
why: Predicting the same price for every house means the model learned nothing about what affects price. That's underfitting.
trap: Memorizing would give very different prices.

prompt: Training stopped after one pass, and the model still misses obvious patterns.
why: One pass of training wasn't enough to learn even the obvious patterns. Stopping too early leaves the model underfitting.

prompt: Accuracy is low even on the data the model trained on.
tells: low even on the data the model trained on
why: If a model can't even do well on its own training data, it's too simple or undertrained. That's underfitting.
trap: Overfit models ace their training data.

prompt: A spam filter that only looks at message length can't tell spam from real mail.
why: Length alone carries too little information to tell spam from real mail. A model without enough to learn from underfits.
trap: It's too simple, not too specific.

prompt: Making the model bigger improves both training and test scores.
tells: improves both training and test scores
why: A bigger model improved both training and test scores, so the smaller one was too simple. It was underfitting.
trap: If it were overfitting, a bigger model would hurt the test score.
